body.statement: For the one-pair chart with \(t^2\asymp\lambda\), let \(P^+_{a,t}\) and \(P^-_{a,t}\) be the two coordinate-swapped orientation laws. Uniformly for \(a\in[a_-,a_+]\), both laws lie in \(\mathcal M_1(\lambda)\), and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) satisfy \[c\lambda\le h^2(P^+_{a,t},P^-_{a,t})\le \operatorname{KL}(P^+_{a,t}\|P^-_{a,t})\le C\lambda.\] The score expansions and density-ratio expansion are uniform under the same fixed envelope.
body.justification: The mirror calculation links the causal margin \(\lambda\) to one-sample testing information without introducing an unrelated divergence assumption.
body.gap: Acharya et al. (2023, Theorems 1.1--1.5) derive intervention--observation tradeoffs for discrete causal-structure identification, and Jin (2026, arXiv:2608.15840v1, Theorem 3.1) derives a bivariate linear-LiNGAM frontier from edge, non-Gaussianity, and scale margins; neither constructs opposite-orientation nonlinear restricted-ANM laws whose fixed-kernel residual-HSIC margin and testing information are both of order \(\lambda\).
body.consumer: The proposition is the legal one-coordinate experiment needed for the product-testing converse.
